fields.meta_title: Custom Order Form Builder for Made-to-Order Work | Emergent
fields.meta_description: A custom order form that quotes every option a buyer picks and holds each job until the buyer approves the proof. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Custom Order Form That Prices Every Choice
fields.hero_description: Build a custom order form that prices each option, collects reference files, and saves every job to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Each Order Carries Before Work Starts
fields.features_subheading: A custom order form prices a one-off job, gathers what it takes to make it, and checks there is room to take it on.
fields.feature_1:
Prices that follow each option

Set a base price and what each choice adds, such as a wood species, an extra foot of length, or a rush date. The buyer watches the total change and submits an order already priced.
fields.feature_2:
Reference files on the order

Ask for room photos or a hand sketch on the same screen as the options. Each file is saved with its order, and the brief opens beside the pictures on the day work begins.
fields.feature_3:
A proof step before work begins

Send a proof or a mockup back to the buyer and hold the order until they approve it or ask for a change. Every revision request and the final yes are logged on the order.
fields.feature_4:
Capacity that closes a full month

Cap how many jobs a month or a week can take. Once a month is full, the form stops offering it and shows the next open one, and buyers only pick dates the maker can keep.
fields.feature_5:
One record per order, start to finish

Each order is a row in a database you own, with its options, files, proof, and status together. Filter by due date to plan the week, or by status to see what waits on a buyer.
fields.feature_6:
Your code, your repository

Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans and keep building it with your own developers. The free tier covers building and publishing the form itself.

fields.tab_content_1:
The quote changes with every wood and length choice

Hollis Creek Woodworks builds dining tables to order. A 6-foot oak table starts at $1,800, walnut adds $600, and the 8-foot length adds $350. Dana Whitfield picks walnut at 8 feet and sees a quote of $2,750 before she submits. Her order arrives with that quote and a photo of her dining room attached.
fields.tab_content_2:
Each ring waits for a yes on its proof

Wren Street Jewelry asks for ring size, metal, and a sketch or photo of the design. Priya Nolan orders a size 7 ring in 14k yellow gold and uploads 2 reference photos. The studio sends back a rendered proof, she approves it on her phone, and only then does the order move to casting.
fields.tab_content_3:
Six commissions fill a month, then it closes

Juniper Lane Portraits paints six pet portraits a month. October and November each have six booked, and the form marks both months full. It offers December, where two of six are booked. Theo Marsh picks December, uploads photos of his cat, and gets a confirmation naming the month his portrait starts.
fields.tab_content_4:
Rush jobs land with Marcus, not the queue

Bright Line Signs prints banners and storefront lettering. Any order needed within 5 business days goes to Marcus Lindqvist, the production manager, as an email he can accept or decline. Copperleaf Dental orders 4 vinyl banners due in 3 business days. Every other job joins the standard queue.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Custom Order Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps turn your options, prices, and capacity into a custom order form that quotes each buyer, built with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List every option and its price
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Decide which files each order needs
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down each choice a buyer makes and what it does to the price: the base item, each material or size upgrade, and any rush fee. Note which options rule out others, such as a finish that only comes in oak.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick the files you need before work can start, such as a room photo or a hand sketch. Mark which ones are required and which are optional, and say what a good photo shows, such as the full wall or the pet in daylight.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Count how many pieces you can finish in a month at your normal pace, with time left for revisions. Set that number as the cap, and decide whether a full month offers the next one or opens a waitlist.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Put your notes from the first three steps into one prompt. Emergent builds the form with its price rules and the database that holds each order. Change any part later by prompting again, such as a new wood or a higher rush fee.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Add the proof and approval step
fields.howto_step_5_des: Say how a proof reaches the buyer and what counts as approval. Keep each order out of production until the buyer approves, and let them ask for a change with a note that stays on the order.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick the jobs that need a person right away, such as anything due within a week or over a set total. Name the person in the rule, and the app sends each match to them by email or Slack with a link to the order.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test with real orders, then publish
fields.howto_step_7_des: Place three test orders yourself: a plain one, one with every upgrade, and a rush job. Check each quote by hand against your price list, then publish the form on its own link or on your custom domain (included in Emergent, uses credits).

faq_plan.q: What is a custom order form?
faq_plan.a: A custom order form is the form a buyer fills in to order something made to their own specification instead of a stock product. It records the options they choose and the price those options add up to, along with reference files and the date they need it by.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a custom order form?
faq_plan.a: List the options a buyer can choose and what each one adds to the price, then the files you need and how many orders you can take in a month. Describe all of that in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder, and it returns a working form with the pricing and a record for every order.

faq_plan.q: What should a custom order form ask the buyer?
faq_plan.hint: How do i create a custom order form using pages?
faq_plan.a: Ask for what you need to price and start the job. That means the product, each option that changes the cost, the quantity, the date it is needed, and a way to reach the buyer. Add a reference upload and a notes box last. Leave out anything you would only need after the buyer approves the quote.

faq_plan.q: Can one custom order form cover several different products?
faq_plan.a: It can, if you build it to ask which product the buyer wants first and then show the options for that product alone. A table buyer never sees ring sizes, and a ring buyer never sees wood species. If you sell one item in a fixed grid of sizes and colors, such as printed shirts, a t shirt order form with a quantity per size is the simpler fit.

faq_plan.q: How does a custom order form work out the price from the options?
faq_plan.a: It starts from a base price and adds or multiplies what each choice changes, such as a material upgrade or a rush fee. Show the running total next to the options, and save the final figure with the order. In a form built with Emergent, you change a price rule by prompting, without rebuilding the form.

faq_plan.q: How do buyers attach photos or sketches to a custom order form?
faq_plan.a: Add an upload field and say exactly what to send, such as the wall with a tape measure in the shot or a sketch with the dimensions written on it. Allow several files per order. Emergent keeps each file next to its quote in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What happens after a buyer submits a custom order form?
faq_plan.a: The order becomes a job with a status that moves as the work does, such as quoted, waiting on proof, approved, in production, and shipped. Give the buyer a confirmation that names the next step. If the job is a repair or a service visit instead of a made item, a work order form tracks it better.

faq_plan.q: How can a custom order form limit how many orders I take each month?
faq_plan.a: It counts each order against a monthly cap you set, closes a month once the cap is reached, and offers the next month or a waitlist. Base the cap on what you finished last month, minus time for revisions. Forms built with Emergent have no response caps, and the only limit is the one you set.

faq_plan.q: How long should a custom order form say an order will take?
faq_plan.a: Give a ship window you can meet from your current queue, and show it before the buyer submits. For most goods ordered by mail, telephone, fax, or on the Internet, the FTC's mail order rule says a seller needs a reasonable basis for any ship time it states. With no statement, the seller needs a reasonable basis for shipping within 30 days.

faq_plan.q: When are custom order forms better than taking orders by message?
faq_plan.a: Custom order forms win once orders carry choices that change the price or need files. A message thread spreads the details across several replies, while a form keeps them in one record. A home baker who takes decorated cookie requests each week might start with a cookie order form instead.

plan.angle: The top 10 is template galleries and order-form creators (Jotform, Cognito, AidaForm, Canva) plus two explainers, and every one of them treats an order as a product list with a quantity box. A custom order has no fixed price or fixed product: the buyer picks options that change the cost, sends reference files, and the maker approves a proof and checks capacity before saying yes. This page shows those four mechanics working in four made-to-order trades: a furniture quote built from wood and length, a ring proof approved before casting, a portrait artist's monthly slots, and rush sign jobs sent to the production manager.
